sections.normalized_html: Let [MATH: z(w) = |25 - 5w|.] For which values of [MATH: k] does [MATH: z(k) = 5k?]
sections.readable_text: Let [MATH: z(w) = |25 - 5w|.] For which values of [MATH: k] does [MATH: z(k) = 5k?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are given the equation [MATH: z(w) = |25 - 5w|] and asked to find the value of [MATH: k] for which [MATH: z(k) = 5k.] Therefore, we need to solve the equation [MATH: |25 - 5k| = 5k.] We now split into two cases based on the definition of absolute value.

  • First, we consider the case where [MATH: 25 - 5k \ge 0.] Then, we have [MATH: |25 - 5k| = 25 - 5k.] Therefore, our absolute value equation becomes [MATH: 25 - 5k = 5k.] Solving the above equation for [MATH: k,] we obtain [MATH: 25 − 5k|= 5k; 25|= 10k; k|= (5)/(2).] Now, we check whether this value of [MATH: k] satisfies the condition for the first case: [MATH: 25 − 5((5)/(2))|= 25 − (25)/(2); = (25)/(2); ≥ 0✓] So, [MATH: k = \dfrac{5}{2}] is a valid solution.

  • Now, we consider the case where [MATH: 25 - 5k < 0.] Then, we have [MATH: |25 - 5k| = -(25 - 5k).] This equation becomes: [MATH: -25 + 5k = 5k \Rightarrow -25 = 0,] which is not true. Therefore, no solution arises from this case.

Thus, the only value that satisfies the equation [MATH: z(k) = 5k] is [MATH: k = \dfrac{5}{2}.]
